#2993. U.S. companies from Nvidia to Apple face a growing China dilemma

BEIJING — How does the U.S. stay ahead of China in the artificial intelligence race? Keep advanced chips out of Beijing's reach, or sell weaker versions to keep Chinese companies reliant on American technology?

The consequences for U.S. businesses came into sharper focus after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, ahead of U.S. President Donald Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping this week.

Huang, who resigned last week amid reports he'd had an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, had argued that keeping U.S. technology available in China could help the U.S. stay ahead in the tech race.

Others want tougher restrictions on chip sales: The Trump administration tightened restrictions on Chinese companies' remote access to advanced U.S. chips on Monday, seeking to prevent them from bypassing export controls by using data centers overseas.

The question facing Nvidia is part of a broader dilemma for U.S. tech companies: how far to remain invested in China as tensions between the two countries put their access to customers and supply chains at risk.

On Sunday, nine countries, including Singapore and the U.K., signed the U.S. State Department's "San Francisco Declaration" to safeguard sensitive technologies.

"Companies operating in China face competing pressures from Washington and Beijing," a client brief from New York-based consulting firm Strategy Risks said following the Nvidia scandal.

"Actions that satisfy one government can create serious problems with the other, putting market access, investments, and corporate reputation at risk," the brief said.

"Executives need to understand and price out these trade-offs before making consequential decisions."

China's economic slowdown and escalating bilateral tensions have made it harder for American businesses there. Few expect Trump and XI to significantly expand on a fragile trade truce achieved last fall.

Huang was among the tech CEOs at the Xi-Trump summits in September and May, but U.S. officials said Trump does not plan to raise the alleged Nvidia spy case during Thursday's meeting. Elon Musk is travelling with the president, who is otherwise not bringing a business delegation as he did in May.

"American tech companies have been diversifying away from China," Kyle Chan, a fellow at The Brookings Institution, told CNBC, but Nvidia and Apple are "in some ways stark outliers against this trend."

Analysts are watching how Apple CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in October, navigates bilateral tensions.

"Ternus may accelerate a process of diversification away from China that Tim Cook started," Chan said. "But it's hard to imagine that China will not play an essential role in Apple's future under Ternus, given the depth and breadth of China's manufacturing supply chains."

Apple still manufactures most of its iPhones in China, and Greater China, which Apple defines as mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, accounts for around 15% of sales.

"The most defensible path is managed decoupling—not the rolling deferrals and hedged announcements that defined Cook's tenure—but a genuine strategic commitment to building a company that can absorb the reductions of China access without losing the ability to manufacture at the cutting edge," Strategy Risks CEO Isaac Stone Fish wrote in American Affairs earlier this year.

China's economic clout, however, also increases the fallout from any retaliation Beijing decides to enact in response to tighter U.S. policy.

Companies, especially U.S. multinationals, pursued the China market after it began re-opening to foreign businesses in the 1980s. Consumer demand boomed, while local factories produced so much they reached 40% of global container exports this summer. The U.S. AI data center buildout relied on China-made parts.

China has amassed control of the supply chain for critical minerals. Beijing has used its grip on rare earths as leverage in trade talks with the U.S. and the EU.

Despite some buildout of the rare earths supply outside China, "it's just not at the scale that the world needs to continue to build products and for industry to continue to evolve," said Cameron Johnson, a Shanghai-based senior partner at business consultancy Tidalwave Solutions.

He cited looming shortages of yttrium, which would limit the production and repair of airplane engines.

"There's just no road map. That's really one of the biggest issues," Johnson said. "Companies have no idea what they're ordering now, whether they will have access to it again."

#2990. NextBoat (NXB) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Revenue more than doubled, but rising interest costs are now in focus.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

NextBoat Inc. (NXB -1.57%) reported record quarterly revenue that more than doubled compared to the prior year, supported by significant growth in pre-owned boat sales and the integration of new boat lines from recent acquisitions. Management indicated that while top-line expansion was strong, the focus has shifted toward margin improvement and operational efficiency to address rising interest and storage costs. The company is implementing new inventory management strategies to reduce carrying times and is integrating its financing arm into every transaction to capture higher-margin service and insurance revenue. Management maintained its full-year revenue outlook and indicated a path toward sustainable profitability through infrastructure development and cost reduction.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the NextBoat 2026 Third Quarter Financial and Operating Results Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] I will now hand the conference over to John Evans, Investor Relations. John, please go ahead.

John Evans: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NextBoat's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. With us today are Ross Tannenbaum, NextBoat's CEO; and Chad Corbin, NextBoat's CFO. Later on, Jason Ruegg, NextBoat's Founder and President, will join us for Q&A. I'd like to start by reminding you that certain comments on this call are forward-looking statements as defined by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Any forward-looking statements speak only as of today. These statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause results to differ materially from expectations.

These risks include, but are not limited to, the impact of seasonality and weather, global economic conditions, the level of consumer spending, the company's ability to capitalize on opportunities or grow its market share and numerous other factors identified in our Form 10-K and other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which can be found on the Investor Relations portion of the company's website. Also on today's call, management will make comments referring to non-GAAP financial measures. Management believes that the inclusion of these financial measures helps investors gain a meaningful understanding of the changes in the company's core operating results.

These measures can also help investors who wish to make comparisons between NextBoat and other companies on both a GAAP and non-GAAP basis. The reconciliation to non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures is available in today's earnings release. The company disclaims any obligation or undertaking to update forward-looking statements to reflect circumstances or events that occur after the date the forward-looking statements are made, except as required by law. Please also note that all comparisons of our third quarter 2026 results are made against the third quarter of 2025 results, unless otherwise noted.

I'd also like to remind everyone that today's call is being recorded, and an archived version of the call will be available on the company's website sometime after the call. With that, I'd like to turn the call over to NextBoat's CFO, Chad Corbin.

Chad Corbin: Thanks, John. Good afternoon, and thank you for joining us. Starting with revenue for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, we generated record third quarter revenue of $50.6 million, representing an increase of 111% compared to the $24 million in the same period of 2025. Revenue grew across all divisions this quarter. We put our floor plan capacity to work, expanded our broker networks at Off The Hook and Autograph Yacht Group and added service and new boat revenue from Apex Marine and Bellhart, both acquired in the second quarter of 2026. Our finance division, Azure, also contributed to revenue growth. The result, higher pre-owned boat sales, more completed brokerage transactions and broader revenue contributions across the business.

New boat sales increased by $5.3 million to $7.5 million for the 3 months ended September 30 compared to the $2.3 million in the same period 2025. The increase is attributable to the new boat lines, which were acquired through Apex Marine and Bellhart acquisitions. Pre-owned boat sales increased by $17 million or 81% to the $37.9 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the $20.9 million in the same period of 2025. For the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, we sold approximately 204 pre-owned units compared to approximately 109 pre-owned units for the same period 2025.

Our pre-owned boat sales encompass a broad range of brands and sizes and include inventory, trade-in, brokerage and consignment transactions. To get a sense of the scale of our brokerage sales, in addition to our company-owned boat sales, we sold $65.7 million worth of brokerage boats in the quarter versus $16 million for the same quarter in 2025. So that means our team sold a total of $103 million in pre-owned boat sales versus $36.9 million for the same quarter in 2025. The number of brokerage boats sold in the quarter was 126 versus 58 boats in the same quarter of 2025.

It is important to note that these brokerage boats can contribute service, financing, insurance and warranty contract revenue as well as brokerage commissions to the company. Revenue from arranging financial products, including financing, insurance, extended warranty contracts to customers through various third-party financial institutions and insurance companies increased to $1.2 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the $600,000 in the same period of 2025. The increase was driven by higher units delivered, incremental business generated by recent strategic hires and a greater focus on warranty sales for our pre-owned units.

Revenue from service parts and other sales increased to $3.9 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $164,000 in the same period of 2025. The increase is attributable to the acquisitions of Apex Marine and Bellhart Marine. These acquisitions have enhanced our in-house inventory services capabilities and supported the expansion of our retail service offerings. Gross profit increased by $3.8 million or 90% to $8 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the $4.2 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was driven by higher boat transaction volumes across our platform. Growth in our higher-margin service and financial product businesses also contributed to our gross profit expansion.

Selling, general and administrative expenses consist primarily of lease expense, insurance, utilities and other customary operating expenses. SG&A increased $1.9 million to $2.5 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the $600,000 in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by operating costs associated with Apex Marine, Autograph Yacht Group and Bellhart and the legal fees and transactional costs associated with those acquisitions, none of which were owned in 2025. These costs were consistent with our planned business expansion for 2026. Salaries and wages expenses increased $4.1 million to $6.9 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the $2.7 million in the same period of 2025.

The increase reflects the impact of acquisitions and investments into personnel to support growth, both leading up to and following our initial public offering. The company's floor plan interest expense increased $434,000 or 103% to $855,000 for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the $421,000 in the same period of 2025. We expect interest expense to remain elevated as we continue to utilize our expanded floor plan credit facility. Net loss attributable to NextBoat Inc. for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $4.6 million compared to a net loss of $100,000 in the prior year quarter. The increase in net loss reflected a $7 million year-over-year increase in total operating expenses.

Included in the third quarter results were $3 million in noncash nonrecurring expenses, of which $1.5 million related to stock-based compensation under the company's employee equity plan. After accounting for these items and the other adjustments detailed in our adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.6 million for the quarter. We are maintaining our full year 2026 revenue guidance of $165 million to $170 million, representing approximately 43% year-over-year growth. Based on our performance to date, we expect to achieve the upper end of this range with the potential to exceed it.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Ross to discuss our third quarter performance highlights and provide an update on our near- and long-term strategic priorities.

Ross Tannenbaum: Thanks, Chad. I want to thank everyone for joining the call today, and I'm very excited to be part of the NextBoat team. We are in the process of fundamentally changing the economics of NextBoat, how we buy, how we sell and every touch point in between. I believe the progress made over the past 30 days represents an important turning point for the company. We have strengthened the leadership team, raised additional capital, renegotiated unfavorable economic arrangements and developed a much clearer strategy for the future. Our objective is to make NextBoat the most efficient buyer and seller of boats in the country.

I would like to spend a few minutes adding some color to the financial results before opening up to questions. I would like to make it very clear. We are now concentrating on margin expansion. We feel very comfortable that we can continue to grow this company. We've got great control over marketing, technology and all the things that we do. But now it's most important to work on all the costs associated with buying and selling boats. I would like to start with the pre-owned sales. As Chad pointed out, we saw 80% revenue growth on the pre-owned side and 98% unit growth.

I think it's important to understand that in the business we're in, revenue growth can be skewed by very large transactions. And so we look very closely at the unit growth. As we move forward, we've also identified that the best boats for us tend to be boats in the $500,000 range and below. We have the best margins in those boats. We have the most potential buyers of those boats, and we seem to have a much clearer understanding of what that market looks like. And so you will see us working very hard to grow that category over time.

And so I would call out that over the next several quarters, starting with our K, we're going to want to pay close attention to unit growth because we believe we can tremendously grow that space, which will add to margin contribution. So how are we going to grow sales? So the biggest part of our strategy is getting back to cutting costs. Today, how we buy boats, what we pay to transport a boat, to store a boat, the insurance, the survey, the selling costs, all are well over what they should be.

And for us to be able to close more transactions, we've got to cut those costs, which would allow us to push more margin, but to also allow us to bid more for a boat and increase our conversion rate on those transactions. Our goal is simple, to become the market for the wholesale side of the business when you want to sell a boat to know that NextBoat is a destination because you're going to get the best offer for your boat. To also accomplish that, that's going to require getting better on how we sell boats.

I truly believe that over the last 6 to 9 months, because of all the acquisitions and the growth since going public, the company got derailed somewhat from the management of its core business, which is buying and selling boats. The addition of Apex, the addition of Bellhart, the launching of AYG, all very important businesses moving forward. But all the effort it took to incorporate those into the company really had an impact on the management of the inventory of owned boats that we had and the process and how we liquidated those boats.

We have already implemented plans that manage that inventory on a daily basis and get much more aggressive in our markdown strategies to ultimately contribute the largest margin. I'll give you an example of how this can really impact the business going forward. In the first 9 months of the year, 6 of our boats made up the biggest losses we took in the entire company. And those losses added up to around $1.5 million. Of those losses, the boats that we purchased, the price of the purchase compared to the price of the sale was breakeven. The average days owned was approaching 1 year. It was over 250 days.

Had we been more aggressive in how we manage that inventory during that time, we could have cut that loss to either 0, potentially made a profit, but a worst-case scenario would have lost a couple of hundred grand instead of $1.5 million. So the impact of better managing inventory and having a better process and how we liquidate the boats will have a big impact on our long-term growth and profitability. I want to touch on Azure for a minute. I think you've heard in previous calls that Azure is an important part of the business. It's the part that is finance, insurance and warranty.

Without proper integration of that into your overall strategy, it's very hard to be a great successful business because we need those revenues and more importantly, we need the earnings and the margin from that. In the past, Azure has kind of run on its own. And although there has been some efforts to try to incorporate that into the overall company at NextBoat, it hasn't been that successful. Well, those days have changed as well. As of the last few weeks, we are now incorporating every transaction to go through Azure so that we can capitalize on finance insurance and warranty. It's part of our closing process and now should have a huge impact.

And even though it grew 97% year-over-year, we think that number could be much, much higher when it's properly integrated. And then finally, I want to touch on service. Service is a very important component of the business as well. It's a high-margin business. But for us, the key to service is actually controlling the work done on our own boats. It's shortening the time it takes to fix a boat. It's keeping the cost down on fixing those boats. The locations offer another place to store boats at a lower price. And it really gives us an opportunity to improve our pricing long term.

And then finally, as it relates to that, the service plays a key component in customer retention. We're going to make sure that every client that we deal with that buys a pre-owned boat for us gets a service opportunity, a service contract. And so we can stay in touch with them to try to make sure they come back to us for their next transaction. And so with that, I'm going to open it up to questions. And if anybody has a question, please raise your hand, and I'll try to address it the best I can.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Mark Smith with Lake Street Capital Markets.

Unknown Analyst: This is [ Alex ] here on for Mark Smith. You guys had $50.8 million of inventory this quarter. How will the company execute on maintaining or potentially improving your inventory turns while also maximizing the Azure revenue?

Ross Tannenbaum: Alex, thanks for joining. Great question. So I want to break out the floor plan a little bit. So the floor plan for our core business, which is the pre-owned boats, is actually a number, I think, around $30 million or slightly below. One of the challenges has been, and I touched on a little bit on the update, is that because of the addition of these other businesses and that you had a leadership team that was being stretched really thin to try to integrate those and also run the business, there's no question that the average days on the boats got longer.

With that being said, I believe today, that average ownership on the pre-owned boats is around 88 days. And as I keep touching on this whole, we've got to impact buying, selling and all the things in between, let me give you like one example of how we can impact that. So when we buy a boat, we contract with the client and then we go through a process of closing on that boat. Historically, we've made that transaction, made that deal, and then it's taken, we call it, a couple of weeks to close, and we're waiting until we close to start doing all the important things like taking photos and detailing and getting listed and selling that boat.

Internally, we've looked at and said, we believe that we can push out the closing date a little bit more, whether it's another week or 2. And during that time, be doing all the things that we would have done after close, which is photograph the boat, clean it again and get it marketed through our internal database. And so we think we can pick up weeks on the front end by just incorporating that. It's kind of the same thing on the back end. The company has also had so many transactions going on that the closing team has been somewhat strapped and it's pushed closings on the sell side out weeks longer than it was necessary.

And so every day that we go past the date that, that deal should close, it costs us money for storage. It costs us money for interest on all those things. And so -- we feel like we can take the 88 days down to some number even into the 60s just by that simple process on the closing side and the buy and sell side. And then the other thing is we had a great addition of Alex Dean to the team, which was announced this week, who's our COO. Alex worked very closely with me, both at my original company and Fanatics.

I don't know anybody stronger than Alex when it comes to operational efficiencies, and Alex has hit the ground running. And every single touch point, we see opportunity to improve that. But the other thing Alex has already started doing is having daily interaction on the inventory list to make sure every day we're assessing what boats should be priced at. We're analyzing all the offers that are coming in, and we're making sure that we're being aggressive in trying to turn boats.

We believe that we can -- by cutting all these costs, we can still increase our margins by reducing the price we sell if necessary sooner because it cuts down all the additional costs like I keep touching on, like interest and storage and everything else. And so of all the things that we're going to do over the next, call it, 120 days to 6 months, I believe you're going to see the biggest impact on the cost of carrying these boats, and you're going to see the turns come down and you're going to see a much better return on those boats because of that.

The other part of the floor plan comes from the new boats that we took on. And so the new boats, which are both at Apex and at Bellhart are going to be a little more seasonal. And so an example is that on the Apex side, we're already seeing a tremendous return after the Fort Lauderdale Boat Show, which is the largest boat show in the world, yet we saw it was kind of slow in the summer. We're down here in Florida where I reside, it's not really a big part of the boat season in the summer as most of the snowbirds go away. But now through, let's call it, May is really boating season here.

And I think you'll see that floor plan come down pretty dramatically as we sell through those boats. At the Bellhart side, which is up in North Carolina, it's kind of the opposite. They just ended their boating season not too long ago, and their boat season will kick up again around, just after the first of the year. And so it will be a little slow now and that floor plan might increase or stay where it is, you'll see that come down pretty dramatically during the boating season up in the Northeast.

Unknown Analyst: Great. And then I know you guys held your $165 million to $170 million revenue guide despite the Q3 results, which kind of implies the year-over-year decline sequentially. Is this deliberate inventory optimization or is this pull forward into Q3 or softer demand? Or any other color there would be appreciated.

Ross Tannenbaum: So I don't know that I understand the question. So yes, you saw what the numbers were through 3 quarters and our guidance is a number $165 million, $170 million. The first answer I'll give you is, I believe we will clearly exceed the guidance. We're being conservative here because we want to -- we don't want to let the cat out of the bag too much. But based on the first 9 months results, it's pretty clear that we're going to, as we talked about, achieve the higher end of the goal or exceed it, and we see that happening.

I will say that what you're also going to see in Q4, and I think this is really important to understand, we feel very comfortable that we can grow revenue very rapidly here, and we feel we can grow it profitably. The bigger challenge right now that exists and the reason for the addition of an Alex Dean on the COO side and other additions we're making internally is we don't want to grow too fast before we can build the infrastructure below that revenue to support it and offer a good customer experience and make sure it's profitable.

Again, when you look at all the touch points involved in this, and everything that's involved to do this right, I feel like we're on the verge of major growth, which would be very difficult to handle and would offer maybe a declining customer experience. I want to make sure in Q4 that we're investing in all of those initiatives to have the foundation as we head into '27 to get aggressive again on our growth as we head into '27. And then the other point you made, we are in the process also of trying to get out of boats that have been in inventory too long and clean up that inventory.

And that happened some in Q3, which had some impact on our ultimate bottom line earnings. And I would think you're going to continue to see that some in Q4 as we kind of realign our goals on what boats are better suited for us and where we can make the most money.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to now turn the call over to Ross for closing remarks.

Ross Tannenbaum: Well, again, I want to thank everybody for joining the call. I think it's a very exciting time for NextBoat. I think, again, when you look at the addition of the people we've added to this team and then you fall back on the expertise of Jason and Blake and the people who have been here for a very long time, it's very clear that they're probably two of the best in this industry in the pre-owned boat market. And so our goal is to build on their experience and their knowledge. And then I want to also point out again that we really believe the key to our future is also driven by digital marketing and technology.

Our technology is pretty amazing when you look at it today, but we've already got a whole list of additions we can add to it to make it that much better. And the more we can expand our technology, I think the more efficient we'll get throughout the entire process, which will also push more to the bottom line. And so with that, I'm going to end the call and say I look forward to finishing Q4. We're always available at this company to talk about how things are going because our shareholders are very important to us. And I look forward to the next communication after we file our K.

Operator: This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#2986. Analysis: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means

Artificial intelligence is about to sweep through the economy. The Federal Reserve is bracing for impact.

"We are at a hinge point in the U.S. economy," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said at a conference he convened in San Francisco on Monday. But exactly when and how the economy could turn, and what that means for interest rates and inflation, isn't yet clear.

The meeting of Warsh's AI task force saw the new Fed chairman publicly asking the questions Americans will ultimately expect him to answer. He hinted at a few of his private views on whether white-collar workers could soon face massive job losses, but he largely left the speculation to an array of experts he has assembled to advise the Fed.

With the technology racing ahead, Warsh won't be able to put off giving his own answers much longer. AI lab Anthropic plans to price the shares for its initial public offering on Wednesday and could raise as much as $64 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Vast spending from AI firms is prompting the Fed to contemplate raising interest rates in December to slow down the rate of price increases as the tech sector heats up the economy.

Meanwhile Americans are souring on some aspects of the technology. The Nov. 3 midterms saw voters enact an array of state-level measures to slow down construction of the data centers that are essential to powering AI.

Warsh moderated three out of four sessions at Monday's event and was involved in selecting the speakers. Among them was one of the few prominent Democrats who was willing to speak out against that anti-data center trend.

It is "a very troubling sign" that so many anti-data center measures passed in the midterms, Gina Raimondo said. She is a former secretary of Commerce under President Joe Biden and a former governor of Rhode Island.

Stopping AI "would be very bad for America" and for the people who voted for the measures, Raimondo said.

Warsh didn't say whether he shares that view, and how it would translate into monetary policy isn't exactly clear.

The event was an unusual one for the Fed. The central bank employs a small army of Ph.D. economists who can rapidly weigh in on anything affecting the U.S. and global economies. But in keeping with his long-standing critiques of the Fed as insular and outdated, Warsh has chosen to draw expertise from outside the institution to help it figure out how to think about what AI will do to productivity and jobs.

Warsh has assembled a task force on that issue, alongside four others devoted to aspects of Fed policymaking.

The public heard Monday from one of the three official members of the task force: venture capitalist Marc Andreessen. Warsh went to Stanford University with Andreessen's wife, and the two have been longtime friends. Another task force member, Stanford economist Chad Jones, is on leave and working at Anthropic and couldn't speak during the company's blackout period ahead of the IPO. The third, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, didn't attend the event.

Andreessen is hugely optimistic about the promise of AI as a technology, but believes the government won't let Americans experience its full effects. Heavy regulation in areas such as healthcare and education mean technology can't replace people's jobs in those sectors, he said.

"To the extent our economy is a free market economy, then maybe you could see the, let's say, extremely rapid displacement scenarios people are talking about," Andreessen said. "But we've mostly outlawed the kind of job transition that … both the utopians the doomers talk about."

Warsh returned repeatedly to one scenario for the economy that draws on past experience. The so-called China shock unfolded after that country joined the World Trade Organization in 2001 and moved heavily into low-cost manufacturing. Americans saw prices on clothing and furniture drop rapidly, for instance, but at the cost of severe job losses. One widely cited estimate found the U.S. lost a million manufacturing jobs and 2.4 million jobs overall in the years that followed.

Warsh suggested to one of the panelists that the widespread adoption of AI might produce its own version of the China shock, this time focused on service workers.

"I don't want to hold this too tightly," Warsh said. "But if in some ways over the last generation or generation and a half, the China shock, for lack of a better word, lowered prices of goods in the United States, the way that I heard you talking about the philosophy of this new technology is it might do something for services."

In other words, AI could do, say, legal or administrative work more cheaply than a human. That could lower prices but put many people out of a job.

Warsh asked panelists whether "we should expect disinflation over the medium term, from what AI could do to services."

They largely suggested it was possible, which could mean the Fed might eventually want to lower interest rates over the long term.

But at the end of the day, it is Warsh and his fellow Fed members who will need to have conviction on the answer.

There are still many steps between the task force discussion and any kind of change in Fed policy. First, the three task force members will have to assemble their points of view into a report for Warsh sometime in the next few months. Then the Fed itself will need to debate those results and decide whether or how to use them to shape monetary policy.

But with AI growing bigger every day, the Fed may need to make up its mind sooner rather than later.

#2983. Omeros (OMER) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

YARTEMLEA gained hospital access as gross product revenue rose 30% this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Omeros Corporation (OMER -18.64%) reported sequential growth in commercial revenue for YARTEMLEA and achieved a second consecutive quarter of positive operating cash flow. Management stated that the commercial launch is focused on educating transplant teams and securing institutional access through pharmacy and therapeutics committee approvals. The company reported that it is implementing strategies to increase outpatient utilization and leverage Medicare reimbursement advantages, such as new technology add-on payments and pass-through status. Additionally, the company indicated it is advancing its clinical pipeline across complement and oncology platforms while managing transition services for its partnership with Novo.

Operator: Good afternoon, and welcome to today's earnings call for Omeros Corporation. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that this call is being recorded at the company's request, and a replay will be available on the company's website. I will now turn the call over to Jennifer Williams, Investor Relations for Omeros. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Cook Williams: Thank you, and good afternoon, everyone. Before we begin, please note that today's discussion will include forward-looking statements. These statements reflect management's current expectations and beliefs as of today and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. For a detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties, please refer to the special note regarding forward-looking statements and the Risk Factors sections in our quarterly report on Form 10-Q filed today with the SEC as well as our most recent annual report on Form 10-K. Today's call will also include a discussion of certain non-GAAP financial measures.

A reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to the corresponding GAAP measures is included in Omeros' earnings press release issued earlier today, which is available on the Investor Relations page of our website and has been furnished with the Form 8-K we filed with the SEC earlier today. With that, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Greg Demopulos, Chairman and CEO of Omeros.

Gregory Demopulos: Thank you, Jennifer, and good afternoon, everyone. Joining me today are David Borges, our Chief Accounting Officer; Dr. Cathy Melfi, our Chief Regulatory Officer; Dr. Steve Whitaker, Vice President of Clinical; and Bill Woodman, our Chief Commercial Officer. I'll begin with an overview of our third quarter operations and financial results, followed by program updates. David will then review the financials in more detail, after which we'll open the call for questions. Following FDA approval in December 2025, we launched YARTEMLEA in late January as the first and only approved treatment for hematopoietic stem cell transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy, or TA-TMA. YARTEMLEA is also the first and only approved inhibitor of the lectin pathway of complement.

The third quarter marked just our second full quarter of YARTEMLEA sales, and we're pleased with our progress. In the third quarter, YARTEMLEA generated $41.8 million in gross sales and $35.9 million in net sales, reflecting continued commercial momentum. Compared with the second quarter, gross sales increased 30%, and net sales increased 26%. As expected, gross to net deductions increased to 14% of gross sales from 11.5% in the second quarter, driven almost entirely by a substantial increase in 340B sales, consistent with our goals of increasing outpatient utilization of YARTEMLEA and expanding our customer base. That momentum has continued into the fourth quarter with YARTEMLEA revenues continuing to grow.

As discussed in prior earnings calls, our reported GAAP financial results include mandatory noncash mark-to-market adjustments associated with the embedded derivative in our 2029 convertible notes. A higher Omeros stock price increases the related noncash expense. Reflecting these noncash adjustments, GAAP net loss for the third quarter was $57.4 million, or $0.79 per share, compared to net income of $13.2 million, or $0.18 per share, in the second quarter. Excluding the noncash remeasurements of the embedded derivatives and other financial instruments, non-GAAP adjusted net income for the third quarter was $4.7 million, or $0.06 per share, compared to second quarter net income of $1.8 million, or $0.02 per share.

We ended the third quarter with $95.3 million in cash and investments. Most importantly, we generated $13.3 million in net cash from operating activities during the quarter, marking our second consecutive quarter of positive operating cash flow. As a reminder, in July, we repurchased $30.5 million in aggregate principal amount of our 2029 convertible notes through two privately negotiated transactions for an aggregate of $60.2 million, reducing the outstanding principal amount by 43% to $40.3 million. These transactions also reduced potential dilution by 4.9 million shares and eliminated $8.6 million in future interest payments. We achieved this reduction at a weighted average cost of $12.21 per underlying conversion share.

Including the repurchase of a little over 843,000 shares of common stock in the open market at $11.70 per share during the first half of 2026, we have reduced the number of outstanding or potentially issuable shares by 5.8 million year-to-date. Let's now look more closely at our YARTEMLEA launch. As we have discussed before, our launch is focused on four priorities: one, educating transplant teams to recognize and treat TA-TMA earlier; two, securing institutional access through pharmacy and therapeutics, or P&T, committee approvals and streamlined ordering; three, ensuring timely and appropriate reimbursement and helping centers understand YARTEMLEA's reimbursement advantages over off-label therapies; and four, demonstrating YARTEMLEA's economic value through health economics and outcomes research, or HEOR.

Through these four priorities, we continue our work to shift clinical practice toward proactive screening for TA-TMA rather than defaulting to a diagnosis of exclusion and toward earlier identification and treatment of more patients with the goal of improving outcomes. To continue advancing these priorities, we have expanded our educational team by adding members to our market development management and medical science liaison teams. This expansion will further strengthen our field medical and educational capabilities and support scientific engagement with health care professionals across transplant centers nationwide. In addition to physicians and pharmacists, we remain focused on supporting nurses.

Nurses spend the most time with transplant patients and are often the first care team members to notice changes suggestive of TA-TMA. For this reason, we recently established a clinical nurse educator team of six nurses from top-tier transplant centers. These Omeros nurses will work directly with nurses and transplant centers across the country. Transplant centers have large nursing teams and staff turnover. New hires and rotating assignments create an ongoing need for training to reinforce recognition of the signs and symptoms of TA-TMA. Our nurse educators will help make TA-TMA awareness part of everyday transplant care, supporting more consistent identification and timely treatment with YARTEMLEA.

So, across our nurse educators, market development managers and medical science liaisons, we have added a total of 10 positions to our field force educational team. To further support our educational efforts, we are adding to our transplant physician, pharmacist and nursing speaker programs by establishing a nephrology speaker bureau comprising both onconephrologists and general nephrologists. Nephrologists are actively involved in the diagnosis and management of TA-TMA. Kidney disease is the most common form of organ dysfunction in TA-TMA. Nephrologists are becoming increasingly well versed in the role of the lectin pathway, and we expect the Nephrology Speaker Bureau will meaningfully expand our educational reach while strengthening understanding of both YARTEMLEA and lectin pathway biology.

Alongside these educational efforts, our field sales team is actively engaging all 175 U.S. transplant centers. As of September 30, 109 unique accounts had ordered YARTEMLEA, a 49% increase from 73 accounts at June 30. Following an outsized share of pediatric utilization in the first quarter, adult adoption accelerated in the second and third quarters. Adult patients now account for approximately 70% of utilization, and pediatric patients for 30%. This mix continues to move toward the historical nationwide allogeneic transplant mix of 85% adult and 15% pediatric procedures. As previously discussed, outpatient use of YARTEMLEA also increased this quarter as evidenced by greater 340B participation. This is good for patients, likely reflective of earlier treatment and potentially better outcomes.

This is also good for transplant centers given that reimbursement for approved drugs in the outpatient setting can range from average selling price, or ASP, plus 4.3% to ASP plus 10% or more. P&T committee approvals also increased by 25% across transplant centers nationwide during the third quarter. By September 30, YARTEMLEA had received P&T committee approvals at 80% of the top 40 U.S. transplant centers nationwide. Let's turn now to reimbursement and the payer experience. To date, all appropriate claims of which we are aware have been paid by commercial payers, Medicare or Medicaid, and coverage is fully aligned with the product label.

And transplant centers are becoming increasingly aware of the new technology add-on payment, or NTAP, for YARTEMLEA, which became effective on October 1. The NTAP provides up to $287,000 in additional Medicare reimbursement per eligible inpatient case involving YARTEMLEA. This is particularly important because Medicare beneficiaries represent approximately 30% of all U.S. allogeneic transplant recipients. No off-label treatment for TA-TMA, whether branded or bio-similar, has an NTAP. This gives YARTEMLEA a distinct reimbursement advantage that can substantially reduce hospitals net cost of treating eligible Medicare inpatients. YARTEMLEA's pass-through status also provides an important reimbursement advantage in the Medicare hospital outpatient setting. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, or CMS, recently issued a new rule on 340B reimbursement.

Beginning January 1, 2027, Medicare will generally reimburse affected hospitals for 340B acquired drugs at average sales price, or ASP, minus 28%. Drugs with transitional pass-through status, however, are exempt from this change and will continue to be reimbursed at ASP plus 6% or ASP plus 4.3% after sequestration. Neither branded eculizumab nor ravulizumab has pass-through status. YARTEMLEA holds pass-through status through June 2029 and is therefore excluded from this reimbursement reduction. This preserves a substantial reimbursement advantage for YARTEMLEA over these branded off-label treatments when purchased under the 340B program and administered in affected Medicare hospital outpatient settings.

In the outpatient setting for commercially insured patients, YARTEMLEA's higher price per dose also translates into greater dollar margins per dose than lower-priced off-label alternatives, whether branded or bio-similar. We believe YARTEMLEA offers better efficacy and safety than off-label treatments for TA-TMA. Now these reimbursement advantages provide centers with additional financial incentives to use YARTEMLEA in both inpatient and outpatient settings. Our HEOR manuscript is being finalized, with journal submission planned within the next few weeks. The analyses show favorable incremental cost effectiveness ratios, or ICERs, for YARTEMLEA compared to best supportive care, eculizumab and ravulizumab. We expect that these analyses will further demonstrate YARTEMLEA's clinical and economic value, supporting its continued adoption.

The recognition of YARTEMLEA's importance to patients and the patient advocacy community is growing. In September, the National Organization for Rare Disorders, or NORD, honored Omeros with its 2026 Industry Innovation Award for YARTEMLEA. NORD is the nation's leading rare disease patient advocacy organization. We are also preparing for a strong presence at the upcoming Annual Congress of the American Society of Hematology, a major international meeting for hematologists and transplant physicians. Dr. Christine Duncan, Associate Professor at Harvard Medical School and Senior Physician at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, will give a podium presentation on the consistent response to YARTEMLEA across three cohorts totaling 71 adult and pediatric patients with high-risk TA-TMA.

Omeros is also sponsoring a continuing medical education session titled Endothelial Injury, Complement, and TA-TMA After Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplant, chaired by Dr. Michelle Schoettler, Associate Professor at Emory University School of Medicine and a pediatric hematologist at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta. The session will examine how TA-TMA has evolved from a historically under-recognized complication with limited treatment options to a disease with increasingly standardized diagnostic criteria, a clearer understanding of its complement biology and now an FDA-approved therapy. The list of YARTEMLEA publications continues to expand. Last month in the journal Bone Marrow Transplantation, a group of international experts reported on a series of severely ill patients with high-risk TA-TMA, all of whom required intensive care unit stays.

Responses to YARTEMLEA among these patients were remarkable. Seven other manuscripts associated and authored by transplant physicians are in preparation or have been submitted, detailing similarly impressive responses to narsoplimab treatment in their patients, including the resolution of organ dysfunction and discontinuation of the need for dialysis. It's gratifying to see this growing body of evidence in both adult and pediatric TA-TMA and supporting these publication efforts remains a corporate priority. Increasing awareness and earlier identification of TA-TMA nationwide, spurred in part by our team's focused educational efforts and growing use and support of YARTEMLEA within the transplant care community, bode well for its adoption as standard of care.

Alongside our U.S. commercial efforts, we are diligently working to expand access internationally. Our initial focus was Europe. As announced in October, the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, or CHMP, following reexamination, which included meetings with CHMP and an ad hoc expert group, or AHEG, issued a negative opinion on our marketing authorization application for narsoplimab for the treatment of TA-TMA. CHMP's process and decision were disappointing and from our perspective, misguided. Separately, due to increasing demand for YARTEMLEA in the U.S. commercial market, we informed CHMP that after 10 years of supplying free drug to Europe and other regions globally under compassionate use, we intend to close the YARTEMLEA compassionate use program to new patients.

TA-TMA patients currently receiving YARTEMLEA through the program will be provided sufficient drug to complete their treatment courses. Our regulatory efforts are currently focused outside the European Union as we work to obtain near-term approvals for YARTEMLEA in TA-TMA across a number of other countries whose regulatory bodies recognize and can build upon the drug's FDA approval. In parallel, we are working to make YARTEMLEA accessible internationally through fully reimbursed named patient programs in parts of Europe and other regions. While pursuing new markets for YARTEMLEA in TA-TMA, we are keenly focused on expanding its indications beyond TA-TMA. Too often, YARTEMLEA is narrowly thought of as a TA-TMA therapeutic. That understates YARTEMLEA's potential. And here's why.

Endothelial injury is central to TA-TMA. Endothelial injury and other cellular damage directly activates the lectin pathway. So, YARTEMLEA, as a lectin pathway inhibitor, has the potential to treat a wide spectrum of disorders driven by endothelial injury. These include other transplant-related disorders such as veno-occlusive disease, capillary leak syndrome, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and graft-versus-host disease. There is substantial interest among transplanters to evaluate YARTEMLEA across these and other indications through investigator-initiated trials. To guide this expansion, we have built a new product planning team that brings insights from clinicians, health systems, payers and patients into our pipeline strategy and related clinical investment decisions.

The three-person team will help identify development opportunities with the strongest clinical and commercial potential to build long-term shareholder value. Two open-label single-arm clinical studies with historical controls evaluating YARTEMLEA are also slated to begin at the end of this year or early next, depending on the timing of Institutional Review Board and ethics committee approvals. One is in acute respiratory distress syndrome, or ARDS, in which endothelial injury is thought to be a key driver of disease. Mortality is high, and there currently is no good treatment for ARDS, which each year affects approximately 190,000 patients in the U.S. alone. The study will assess YARTEMLEA in hyperinflammatory ARDS, which represents about 35% of all ARDS patients.

The second will assess YARTEMLEA's ability to prevent TA-TMA in high-risk pediatric transplant patients. Each study is designed to enroll approximately 50 to 60 patients. Beyond YARTEMLEA, we are advancing the other assets in our MASP-2 platform, our Phase II-ready long-acting MASP-2 antibody, OMS1029 and our oral MASP-2 small molecule program. Both are well suited for chronic indications, with OMS1029 administered once quarterly intravenously or subcutaneously and our oral agent targeting once daily dosing. Where possible, we target an orphan indication that includes a pediatric component as the first indication for a new molecule potentially qualifying for a valuable rare pediatric priority review voucher upon FDA approval, subject to the program's eligibility and timing requirements.

We are finalizing the initial Phase II indication for once quarterly OMS1029, and clinical drug product and matching placebo have been manufactured and are available for Phase II clinical trials. Moving on from our MASP-2 platform, we expect our MASP-3 inhibitor program, the other part of our complement franchise, to generate additional revenue soon. Our collaboration with Novo remains on track. At the closing of the transaction in late 2025, we received an upfront payment of $240 million. In addition, we remain eligible for more than $1.8 billion in development and commercial milestones, including $100 million in near-term milestone payments plus tiered royalties on net sales.

We continue to provide transition services to Novo at Novo's cost and expect to complete those services by mid-2027. In the meantime, we continue to advance our MASP-3 small molecule program toward the clinic. Let's now turn to our pipeline programs beyond our complement inhibitor franchise. Our PDE7 inhibitor program evaluating OMS527 for cocaine use disorder remains fully funded by a grant from the National Institute on Drug Abuse, or NIDA. Earlier this year, we met with FDA regarding the agency's request for additional nonclinical information before initiating the inpatient study in cocaine users. That nonclinical work is underway and expected to be completed this month.

The contract research organization conducting the nonclinical study faced delays in acquiring the study animals. So, we now expect to begin enrollment in the inpatient clinical trial in early 2027 following the upcoming holidays. We still expect data from the clinical trial in 2027. Based on its mechanism of action and our extensive preclinical data, we believe that OMS527 could be effective across a wide range of addiction and compulsive disorders. Our targeted complement activating therapy or TCAP platform is a novel class of recombinant engineered antibodies designed to target and directly kill pathogens, including bacteria, fungi, viruses and parasites.

These antibodies initiate complement activation directly on pathogen surfaces, thereby completely bypassing the classical pathway initiation complex, which pathogens typically exploit to escape immune clearance. Our initial focus is multidrug-resistant organisms, or MDROs, which pose a critical unmet medical need. Unlike conventional antimicrobials, TCAP is designed to eradicate pathogens regardless of resistance profile without promoting new drug resistance. In translationally relevant murine models of sepsis and pneumonia caused by multiple drug-resistant bacterial species, a single dose of the respective TCAP monoclonal antibody demonstrated complete protection and bacterial clearance. IND-enabling studies have begun, and we look forward to advancing TCAP into the clinic. Lastly, OncotoX AML, or OMS805, is the lead program in our oncology platform.

OMS805 is an engineered biologic developed to treat acute myeloid leukemia or AML, the most common and deadliest acute leukemia in adults. In both in vitro studies and studies in tumor-bearing animal models across a diverse range of human AML cell lines, OMS805 consistently demonstrated superior efficacy compared to current standard of care treatments. This potent antitumor activity occurs even at very low doses and across mutations such as those in TP53 and FLT3, which historically have been associated with poor outcomes and treatment resistance. In immunocompetent nonhuman primates, a single course of OncotoX AML achieved a selective, reversible and dose-dependent reduction in target myeloid progenitor cells by up to 99%.

OncotoX AML was well tolerated, demonstrating an encouraging safety profile that preserved essential hematopoietic stem cells without causing broader hematologic toxicity. To support upcoming clinical development, process engineering and initial clinical scale manufacturing are already underway. We have partnered with a leading contract biologics manufacturer to secure initial clinical drug supply and support clinical entry as IND-enabling studies conclude. Working with our Advisory Board of leading AML experts, we are preparing for a first-in-human trial targeted for late 2027. As previously discussed, we are advancing OMS805 in stealth mode and do not plan to provide regular updates. We expect to announce the start of the Phase Ib trial and share clinical data when available.

That concludes our corporate and development program update. Before moving on to our financial discussion, I'd like to welcome Joe Schocken, who joined our Board of Directors and Audit Committee in August. Joe brings decades of experience in investment banking, business leadership and economic policy. He founded Seattle-based investment bank, Broadmark Capital and cofounded and chaired publicly traded Broadmark Realty Capital. A major contributor to the JOBS Act, Joe was also appointed by President Obama to the National Advisory Council on Innovation and Entrepreneurship. We look forward to benefiting from his capital markets expertise, his business experience and his policy perspective.

Now, with that, I'll turn the call over to David Borges, our Chief Accounting Officer, for a detailed discussion of our financial results. David?

David Borges: Thanks, Greg. Our third quarter results reflect continued progress in the commercial launch of YARTEMLEA, along with actions to strengthen our capital structure and enhance our financial flexibility. Excluding noncash remeasurement adjustments associated with our financial instruments, non-GAAP adjusted net income increased 161% from the second quarter, reflecting continued improvement in our financial performance. YARTEMLEA continued to demonstrate strong commercial momentum in the third quarter with gross product revenues increasing to $41.8 million compared to $32.2 million in the second quarter. Net product revenues increased to $35.9 million, up from $28.5 million in the second quarter. Gross to net adjustments were 14% in the third quarter compared with 11.5% in the second quarter and remained within our expectations.

These adjustments consisted primarily of chargebacks and distribution fees with the increase driven primarily by higher utilization of the 340B program. Turning to our financial results. The net loss for the third quarter was $57.4 million, or $0.79 per share, compared to net income of $13.2 million, or $0.18 per share, in the second quarter. These adjustments were driven largely by increases in our stock price in the third quarter.

These noncash adjustments do not affect our operating performance or liquidity and are excluded from our non-GAAP adjusted results. Excluding noncash remeasurements of embedded derivatives and other financial instruments, non-GAAP adjusted net income for the third quarter was $4.7 million, or $0.06 per share, compared to $1.8 million, or $0.02 per share, for the second quarter. In June and July, we entered into 2 privately negotiated transactions to repurchase $30.5 million aggregate principal amount of our 2029 convertible notes for $60.2 million plus accrued interest. Both transactions closed in July, reducing the outstanding principal by 43% from $70.8 million to $40.3 million.

These transactions also reduced future cash interest expense and potential dilution, with the number of shares issuable upon conversion declining from $11.4 million to $6.5 million. We may opportunistically repurchase additional notes in the future depending on market conditions and other considerations. In connection with the second tranche of these repurchases involving $14.5 million in principal, we recorded a $1.9 million loss in the third quarter, reflecting the extinguishment of the repurchased notes and the associated embedded derivative liability. As of September 30, 2026, we had $95.3 million in cash and investments and net cash provided by operations in the third quarter was $13.3 million.

Our cash balance reflects the $60.2 million paid to repurchase a portion of the 2029 convertible notes. Total operating expenses from continuing operations before interest and other income were $31.4 million, an increase of $3 million from the second quarter. Under our transition services agreement with Novo, we continue to receive reimbursements for incurred costs, including third-party expenses and internal personnel costs. We also recognized $459,000 in reimbursements for zaltenibart inventory transferred during the quarter, which was recorded in other income. Interest expense was $6.2 million, consisting primarily of the DRI royalty obligation and interest on the 2029 convertible notes.

Excluding the OMIDRIA royalty obligation to DRI, which is fully offset by amounts received from Rayner and, therefore, has no economic impact on Omeros, as well as noncash amortization of debt issuance costs and discounts, contractual cash interest expense was $1.1 million. This represents a decrease of $600,000 from the second quarter reflecting the impact of our repurchases of the 2029 convertible notes. Interest and other income totaled $1.9 million in the third quarter. And income from discontinued operations was $6.5 million in the third quarter, which was consistent with the second quarter. Because U.S. OMIDRIA royalties are passed directly to DRI, fluctuations in these payments have no impact on our cash position.

Now let me turn to our expectations for the fourth quarter of 2026. We expect total operating expenses from continuing operations to be slightly higher than in the third quarter. Research and development expenses are expected to increase primarily due to higher spending on YARTEMLEA and our OMS805 OncotoX AML program. Sales and marketing expenses also are expected to increase, reflecting continued investment in YARTEMLEA commercial infrastructure, marketing and launch activities. Interest and other income is expected to increase in the fourth quarter, primarily reflecting anticipated inventory reimbursements from Novo. Interest expense is expected to be approximately $6 million, reflecting the reduction in outstanding debt following the 2029 note repurchases.

This estimate excludes potential noncash adjustments related to the OMIDRIA royalty obligation. Income from discontinued operations is expected to be between $5 million and $6 million, excluding noncash remeasurement adjustments related to the OMIDRIA contract royalty asset. Again, these adjustments can be volatile, driven primarily by changes in our stock price and are excluded from our non-GAAP adjusted results. And with that, I'll turn it back over to Greg.
